claims.text: At high temperatures, FeNiCrCoCu thin-film wear resistance is predominantly governed by in-situ formation of a protective oxide scale through tribo-oxidation.
An adherent oxide scale reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and abrasive wear.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu film has a fine-grained microstructure and nominally clean surface.
Pre-annealing FeNiCrCoCu in air near 700 °C for a short duration will promote a nascent protective oxide layer.
The proposed wear regime is approximately 500–900 °C.
Moderate-to-high normal loads are representative of industrial protective-coating applications.
The structural mediator is a continuous, adherent oxide film on the FeNiCrCoCu surface.
The protective film may be a mixed spinel or a similar complex oxide.
Elevated temperature accelerates tribo-oxidation at the sliding interface.
A stable interfacial oxide layer reduces friction and wear.
The oxide layer protects the coating from severe plastic deformation and abrasive damage by acting as a physical and chemical barrier.
At high test temperature, pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu will have lower wear volume than an as-deposited coating tested under otherwise identical conditions.
At high test temperature, pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu will have a lower coefficient of friction than an as-deposited coating tested under otherwise identical conditions.
A protective oxide scale will persist on the worn surface of the pre-annealed coating.
The room-temperature as-deposited baseline has higher wear than the coating in the proposed high-temperature regime.
Higher baseline wear is caused by direct contact and insufficient tribo-oxidation.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply at extremely high loads because such loads disrupt oxide adhesion.
The exact composition, microstructure, and formation kinetics of the protective oxide on FeNiCrCoCu are not fully characterized.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as an as-deposited coating operating at room temperature, whereas the prediction and falsification experiment require the as-deposited control to be tested at the same 700–900 °C temperature as the pre-annealed coating. The hypothesis therefore gives inconsistent baseline conditions.
